mutation_selfcheck.history: three matrices ran. The first (mutation_selfcheck_w1201.json) reported 6 caught, 1 survived and 3 cases whose hard-coded anchors no longer matched, so those cases never ran; the second (round2) tightened anchors to runtime lookup and the refusal assertions to the message each rule produces, reaching 10 caught / 0 survived; the third (round3) adds T11 (exposure forgets the unresolved liability) and T12 (run admission consults no budget policy), which is the case that can only die to the start-time assertion this card owed the round-1 review, and reaches 12 caught / 0 survived. Round4 adds T13, the disjunction turned into a conjunction, which only the new ESTIMATED/BLOCK assertion can kill, and reaches 13 caught / 0 survived. The equivalence probe E1 drops the STRICT term and kills nothing, because no legal policy carries STRICT without BLOCK; it is filed under equivalence_probe so no sensitivity claim rests on a mutant that cannot be distinguished. Every killed id is read from the matrix file, never typed here.
